title: L5: Byte Brawlers Practice
description: Practise the binary sprint, binary and hexadecimal conversions, and clothing drawing tools before the class design contest.

steps.title: Binary Sprint
steps.content:
Practice Mode: binary sprint

In the class contest, this sprint decides how many topic ideas you can submit. You will have 30 seconds to convert as many 4-bit binary numbers into denary as possible.

  • 1 correct answer unlocks 1 topic slot.
  • 3 correct answers unlock 2 topic slots.
  • 7 correct answers unlock 3 topic slots.
  • 15 correct answers unlock 4 topic slots.

steps.title: Binary Place Values
steps.content:
Binary place values

Binary is base 2. Each column is worth double the column to its right. A 1 means use that column value. A 0 means ignore that column value.

1286432168421
01010010

01010010 = 64 + 16 + 2 = 82

Every binary-to-denary conversion uses the same rule: find the columns with a 1, then add those place values.

steps.title: Hexadecimal Digits
steps.content:
Hexadecimal digits

Hexadecimal is base 16. A single hex digit can store any value from 0 to 15. After 9, hex uses letters.

Denary0123456789101112131415
Hex0123456789ABCDEF

A is 10, B is 11, C is 12, D is 13, E is 14 and F is 15.

steps.title: Four Bits to One Hex Digit
steps.content:
Four bits make one hex digit

A group of 4 bits is called a nibble. One nibble can store 0-15, exactly the same range as one hex digit.

steps.title: Two-Digit Hex Values
steps.content:
Two-digit hex values

Two hex digits can represent a whole byte. The left hex digit is worth sixteens. The right hex digit is worth ones.

16s column1s column
5A
5 x 16 = 80A = 10

5A = 80 + 10 = 90

A byte is 8 bits, so it can be written as two nibbles. Each nibble becomes one hex digit.

steps.title: Final Conversion Checkpoint
steps.content:
Final checkpoint before free draw

Answer a mix of binary, denary and hexadecimal questions. This checks that you can convert in every direction you need for Byte Brawlers.

steps.title: Free Draw
steps.content:
Practice Mode: free draw

Choose a clothing template, then practise drawing on it. This is the same canvas used in the contest: type a 4-bit binary code to select a colour, then use the brush, line, fill, eraser, and calculator tools.
